newsitem.title: UK: LME copper hits ceiling, but still ends firmer.
newsitem.headline: LME copper hits ceiling, but still ends firmer.

text.p: Copper ended in the plus column above the psychological $2,500 level on Wednesday, although early momentum dwindled after prices touched new one-year highs.
Three months metal finished the PM kerb $13 stronger at $2,506 per tonnes after stalling at a high of $2,518.

The advance, building on a fund-buying and short-covering rally earlier this week, was eyed with caution by traders and analysts who noted the market was in overbought territory and probably due for a correction.
"There was a lot of selling waiting overhead at $2,415 today," a trader said. But all in all it's not a bad close."

In tandem, the cash to threes backwardation also flared out to around $85/$90 at one point, from around $70 at the end of business on Tuesday. Cash/threes then contracted slightly to $81/$85 by the end of the kerb.
Other base metals, most of which had climbed higher with copper in the morning and earlier this week, ended up with pared gains after initially trying the upside.
Aluminium was barely firmer at $1,652, up just $5.
The market has been underperforming copper in recent days and was unable to hold onto the day's high of $1,668.
A spate of borrowing, however, tightened the cash/threes from a $19 contango on Tuesday afternoon to $13/$10 by the end of the day.
Lead, which leaped to $648 in a speculative, copper-led rally earlier in the day, followed suit and slid off its highs by the end of the kerb.
But it was still a solid $14 higher at $637.
Nickel tumbled sharply by $130 to $7,560, filling a chart gap between $7,620 and $7,660 which was left when prices initially rallied above $2,500 two weeks ago.
"Everything except copper basically gave up the ghost by the end of the day. Nickel really was the worst hit with trade selling taking it down today and yesterday," a trader said.
"Funds and specs had been buying the stuff but they can't hold it forever and have had to stop out," he added.
On the downside the 10-day moving average at $7,614 would probably offer some support, traders said.
The other metals were unremarkable, with tin ending the day at a $35 lower $5,755.
